findings.severity: medium: before the story or any new image path goes public; recommended before HD_PUBLIC=1
findings.what: check:rights recognises a supplier picture only by its path (a file under media/products/, or text naming products/<id>/(photo|opt-…).<w>.webp). The same picture under another name (R2, og:image), a hotlink to the supplier's CDN (R3, ae01.alicdn.com), an inlined data: URI (R4), or the story's own re-encoded copies (R6: 321 files under media/story/products, which the flag build ships today) all pass the gate with exit 0. My scan finds every one. Today's public build ships none, because the story is removed from it.
findings.fix: Make the gate content-based: (1) the pipeline writes the hash of every supplier-derived file (shop and story, every width) and of every cached original; any dist file with one of those hashes fails; (2) a perceptual check of every dist raster and data: URI against the supplier set (dHash 16×16, Hamming ≤ 24 found all 321 story copies with 0 false positives on 169 renders); (3) fail on any URL on a card-picture host (ae01.alicdn.com, cf/oss-cf.cjdropshipping.com, file.zendrop.com, …); (4) make-story applies the same rights rule before the story leaves the flag.

findings.what: The ת38 scrub masks Hebrew runs and quoted text only. Logged as is: a customer's details typed in Latin letters inside an exception's message (request.unhandled: 'Orna', 'Bodeket', 'Sderot HaBodkim', 'Mitzpe Bdika'), phones written 972… or 00972… without '+', and a provider error's own `code` field ('invalid_consignee:Orna' passes errorCode's pattern). The checkout accepts Latin names.
findings.fix: When the order is known, scrub its own customer values (exact match, case-insensitive, both scripts, digits-only phone forms) from any message; otherwise log the error's name and code only in production; PHONE_RE also for 972/00972 without '+'; errorCode takes `code` only from our own error classes or system codes (e.g. ^E[A-Z]+$), never free text.

findings.what: /healthz misses a retry that dies mid-call: the shipment stays 'submitting' with last_error from an earlier failure, which is neither 'stalled' (needs last_error IS NULL) nor 'failing' (needs queued or failed). 90 minutes later: 200 ok, the order still paid and never sent.
findings.fix: Count a 'submitting' shipment older than the lease (10 min) as failing (or drop `last_error IS NULL` from the stall query).

findings.severity: medium, before a real supplier adapter (3.1)
findings.what: A retry after a submit that may have reached the supplier (reach 'maybe') submits again without asking: in B4d the supplier held 2 orders for one of ours (timeout, 503, success). findOrder now exists in the interface, but only the cancellation uses it. The runbook's open question (does CJ reject a duplicate by our order number) decides the risk.
findings.fix: In processSupplierJob, when reach is 'maybe': ask first (findOrder: found → record submitted; none → submit); a supplier that cannot be asked is submitted again only if its adapter documents deduplication by our order number, else the order waits for a person, as the cancellation does.

findings.what: (a) The deploy guard's `npx tsx scripts/check-config.ts`, run from a directory without site/node_modules, downloads tsx@latest from the npm registry and executes it before it fails closed (observed: tsx@4.23.15 into ~/.npm/_npx). (b) The guard reads the file only: `wrangler deploy --env production --var SUPPLIER_PROVIDER:CJ` passes it and deploys the override (dry run); the run-time closed list then refuses it loudly (ת17).
findings.fix: `npx --no-install tsx` (or `node ../node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs`) with `build.cwd` pinned to the config's folder; in the runbook: a provider is never set with --var or a secret.
